summary: The two root causes named in the finding are fixed in 60633eff3 for the standard and desktop builds. Sidebar no longer subscribes to environmentStateById: it uses useShallow(selectCacheHydratedEnvironmentIds). The grouping settings are selected field by field and memoized. Sidebar compiles under the React Compiler (I re-ran the compiler in memory: Sidebar, FrozenWhileHidden and SidebarThreadJumpHintController compile with 0 errors). A browser test asserts zero Sidebar renders for 30 streaming thread.message-sent commits at 2,000 threads. Two gaps keep this from DONE. (1) Fix (3) does not hold. renderProjectRow is wrapped in useCallback, but one of its deps, handleNewThread, is a new function on every Sidebar render. It comes from useNewThreadState, which the React Compiler skips ('Unsupported declaration type for hoisting', the same at f1be4abc7), and that hook still uses the object-returning inline useSettings selector this finding flagged. So every legitimate Sidebar render re-renders SidebarProjectsContent, all memoized SidebarProjectItems, the SidebarWorktreeLists, SidebarChatList and SidebarPrimaryActions. A legitimate render happens, for example, on each coalesced shell upsert, at most 4 Hz per streaming thread. (2) The hosted (Hub web) build has a separate path with the same symptom. The hosted coordinator subscribes to every store commit and republishes a brand-new HostedWorkspaceSnapshot at most every 100 ms. Sidebar subscribes to the whole snapshot. inboxEnvironments and deliveryUnknownThreadKeys therefore get new identities, and InboxSidebar rebuilds its model up to 10 times per second during streaming, even when nothing the sidebar shows has changed. The browser test covers neither case: it runs only in projects mode (the default is inbox), only in the standard build, and only on unrelated commits.

evidence.note: Confirmed fix (1): useStore(useShallow(selectCacheHydratedEnvironmentIds)) plus a memoized Set replaces the whole environmentStateById subscription. selectCacheHydratedEnvironmentIds is at packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts:3422-3428.
Confirmed fix (2): module-level field selectors, and projectGroupingSettings is a useMemo over the two fields. useLogicalProjectSnapshots.ts:47-54 uses the same pattern.

The slice-memoized selectors keep the projects, sidebarThreads and sidebarWorktrees identities when a thread.message-sent commit only touches messageByThreadId, threadTurnStateById or threadShellById. The test therefore discriminates: commitEnvironmentState still creates a new environmentStateById, so the old subscription would fail it.

Defect in fix (3). useNewThreadState fails React Compiler compilation (an in-memory babel-plugin-react-compiler run gives 4x 'Unsupported declaration type for hoisting' at :85; the same happens at f1be4abc7 and 60633eff3), so it runs uncompiled. Its useSettings((settings) => ({...})) inline selector returns a new object on every render (see useSyncExternalStoreSelector.ts:37-48), and handleNewThread's useCallback lists projectGroupingSettings as a dep (:419). handleNewThread is therefore new on every render. useThreadActions.ts:121-126 even says handleNewThread is 'inherently unstable'.

handleNewThread from useNewThreadHandler is a dep of renderProjectRow (:1453) and is passed directly to every SidebarProjectItem (:1428) and to SidebarChatList (:1532). startNewThreadFromSidebar, which goes to SidebarPrimaryActions as onNewThread, also depends on it. The comment at :1414 says renderProjectRow is 'Stable so SidebarProjectsContent (memo) and its sortable rows skip re-rendering', but that is false whenever Sidebar renders. In SidebarProjectItem the new handleNewThread flows into createThreadForProjectMember and createThreadInWorktree (useSidebarThreadActions.ts:316, SidebarProjectItem.tsx:341-351, :524), so each git project's SidebarWorktreeList re-renders too.

Shell thread upserts are now coalesced to 250 ms per thread, so Sidebar legitimately re-renders up to about 4 Hz per streaming thread. On each of those renders the unstable handleNewThread re-renders all 30 project items instead of only the affected one.

Hosted path with the same symptom. useStore.subscribe(scheduleLiveSnapshotPublish) fires on every store commit. Within 100 ms it rebuilds each machine's metadata snapshot (readWorkspaceMetadataSnapshot is O(threads), and an IndexedDB cache.replace follows) and calls publish(machines). publish always builds a new snapshot object, including buildUnifiedWorkspaceIndex and a new demand object. publishHostedWorkspace notifies every listener without an equality check. The same code is in 7bc39eec3, the Ryco revision the Hub vendors.

Sidebar reads the whole snapshot with useHostedWorkspaceState(). inboxEnvironments lists hostedWorkspace as a dep, and deliveryUnknownThreadKeys depends on hostedWorkspace.workspace.threads, which is a new array on each publish. Both get new identities at up to 10 Hz on unrelated commits. They feed ConnectedInboxSidebar, so the InboxSidebar.tsx:123-150 model rebuilds, and they also feed SidebarPrimaryActions. The finding measured that rebuild at about 14 ms warm at 2,000 threads, and inbox is the default mode (uiStateStore.ts:140).

Coverage gap. The test forces sidebarMode 'projects', runs only the standard build (where useHostedWorkspaceState is the signed-out stub), and asserts only that Sidebar does not render on unrelated commits. It does not check that children stay memoized when Sidebar renders legitimately.

The compiler guard covers Sidebar, the inbox components and useSettings, but not useHandleNewThread.ts (useNewThreadState) or useThreadActions.ts, which also fails ('Cannot access refs during render' at :112, though its callbacks have stable deps). Both are hooks that Sidebar calls on every render.

remaining: (1) handleNewThread from useNewThreadHandler (apps/web/src/hooks/useHandleNewThread.ts:85-421) is a new function on every render. The cause is the compiler bailout plus the inline object selector at :96-99, with projectGroupingSettings as a dep at :419. This invalidates renderProjectRow (Sidebar.tsx:1416-1460) and the handleNewThread props at Sidebar.tsx:1428 and :1532. Every legitimate Sidebar render then re-renders SidebarProjectsContent, all SidebarProjectItems, their SidebarWorktreeLists, SidebarChatList and SidebarPrimaryActions. (2) In the hosted build, scheduleLiveSnapshotPublish (hostedConnectionCoordinator.ts:845-877, subscribed at :912) republishes a fresh HostedWorkspaceSnapshot at up to 10 Hz on any store commit. Sidebar.tsx:437 subscribes to the whole object, so Sidebar re-renders and rebuilds inboxEnvironments (:466-603), deliveryUnknownThreadKeys (:604-620) and the InboxSidebar model on commits that change nothing it shows. (3) The browser test does not cover inbox mode, the hosted build, or child stability on legitimate renders.
fixDefects: Fix (3) is ineffective. renderProjectRow's useCallback (Sidebar.tsx:1416-1460) depends on handleNewThread, and handleNewThread changes identity on every Sidebar render because useNewThreadState (useHandleNewThread.ts:85) is skipped by the React Compiler and builds projectGroupingSettings through an inline object-returning useSettings selector (:96-99). The comment claiming renderProjectRow is stable is therefore wrong. The original verifier's correction that the SidebarProjectItems get stable props was also wrong for the same reason, but at the time it only mattered on unrelated commits, which no longer re-render Sidebar. The hosted republish path is a code path the fix did not cover. The auditor's 'None seen' is incorrect.
implementationSketch: A. Stabilize handleNewThread (S, low risk): In apps/web/src/hooks/useHandleNewThread.ts, replace the inline useSettings object selectors in useNewThreadState (:96-99) and useHandleNewThread (:492-495) with module-level field selectors combined by useMemo, the same pattern as Sidebar.tsx:240-249/369-380 and useLogicalProjectSnapshots.ts:22-54. Fix the compiler bailout in useNewThreadState. The likely culprit is the self-recursive named function expressions inside useCallback (useCallback(function handleNewThread(...) { ... return handleNewThread(...) }) and likewise handleNewChat). Recurse through an inner local helper defined inside the callback body instead. Bisect against the in-memory compiler run until useNewThreadState reports CompileSuccess. Add { file: '../hooks/useHandleNewThread.ts', functions: ['useNewThreadState', 'useNewThreadHandler'] } to HOT_COMPONENTS in apps/web/src/perf/reactCompilerCoverage.test.ts. Optionally fix useThreadActions' render-time ref write (:125-126) with a useLayoutEffect, like ConnectedInboxSidebar.tsx:56-62, and add it to the guard as well. Extend Sidebar.renders.browser.tsx: add usePerfMark('SidebarProjectItem') in SidebarProjectItem (the existing mock already counts labels). Then apply a shell change to one thread, e.g. syncServerShellSnapshot with thread-7's updatedAt bumped, or a thread-upserted shell event. Assert that Sidebar renders once and that SidebarProjectItem renders at most once, for project-7 only. B. Hosted narrowing (S, low risk, UI-only): In apps/web/src/hostedHub/hostedConnectionCoordinator.ts, add useHostedWorkspaceSelector<T>(selector, isEqual?) built on apps/web/src/hooks/useSyncExternalStoreSelector.ts with the existing listener set. Add a matching export to hostedConnectionCoordinator.standard.ts that returns selector(SIGNED_OUT_WORKSPACE), keeping the pinned signature. In Sidebar.tsx:437, select only status, machines, demand.queuedEnvironmentIds and the delivery-unknown thread keys. machines is identity-stable across live publishes because scheduleLiveSnapshotPublish passes hostedWorkspaceSnapshot.machines through. queuedEnvironmentIds is stable between coordinator applies (:156, :174). For the delivery-unknown keys, select a sorted string[] compared with a shallow array equality. Rewrite the inboxEnvironments and deliveryUnknownThreadKeys deps to use these values. Do not dedupe inside publish(): it also drives hostedMutationLeaseAuthority.update with the snapshot generation, which is hosted-lifecycle territory. The same narrowing would help ChatView.tsx:639, useHandleNewThread.ts:524 and ProjectSwitcher.tsx:92, which also re-render at up to 10 Hz in hosted mode. Test: add a variant of Sidebar.renders.browser.tsx, or a focused test that mocks hostedConnectionCoordinator with a controllable listener set. Publish a new snapshot object that reuses machines and queued ids, and assert zero Sidebar renders. Also add an inbox-mode run of the existing streaming test.
decisionReason: Both fixes are client-side memoization and subscription narrowing. They do not change auth, relay, readiness or mutation-lease semantics. The one tempting alternative, skipping or deduping the hosted coordinator's publish() or the snapshot refresh, would change the snapshot generation that feeds hostedMutationLeaseAuthority. That falls under AGENTS.md's hosted lifecycle ownership rules and would need owner sign-off, so the sketch deliberately narrows the Sidebar subscription instead.
